newsitem.title: USA: US jobs market weaker in Sept-Labor Dept economist.
newsitem.headline: US jobs market weaker in Sept-Labor Dept economist.

text.p: September payroll data showed a weaker labor market throughout the economy, U.S. Labor Department economist Harvey Hamel said Friday.

"I think the numbers ... show a weaker labor market throughout the economy, whether one looks at the payroll number, which is down 40 (thousand), which we consider essentially unchanged from the August level, or whether you look at the data from our household survey. ... Basically I'd say that very little happened, and it clearly shows weakness. ... There's no question that the September data are weaker," Hamel told Reuters Financial Television.

Hamel said private employment had slowed. An 11-cents-an-hour increase in hourly earnings over August and September showed an increasing trend, although a slight drop in July brought the total third quarter increase to nine cents, which, although "not terribly high," was still a 3.5 percent increase over the same quarter last year.
He said it was hard to predict what effect this month's rise in the official minimum wage would have on jobs data.
Last month's Hurricane Fran, which hit the eastern seaboard, had affected the construction sector, he said.
